g.text: Sample Spaces, Kolmogorov Axioms, Venn Inclusion-Exclusion, Multi-Dice Symmetry, Conditional Chain Rules & Bayes Inversion
• Deterministic: Identical initial conditions ⟹ exact outcome.
• Random: Known set of possibilities S, uncertain individual trial.
TRAP: If P(A), P(B) > 0, Disjoint events are NEVER independent!
Axiom I (Non-negativity): P(E) ≥ 0 for every event E ⊆ S.
Axiom II (Certainty): P(S) = 1, P(∅) = 0. Range: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1.
Axiom III (Countable Additivity): For pairwise disjoint events E₁, E₂, ... :
P( ⋃ Eᵢ ) = ∑ P(Eᵢ) ⟹ P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) if A ∩ B = ∅
• For n fair dice: Min Sum = n, Max Sum = 6n. Center: S_mid = 3.5n.
Symmetry Law: P(Sum = S_mid - k) = P(Sum = S_mid + k) identically.
Two Dice (n=2): P(Sum = s) = (6 - |s - 7|) / 36 for s ∈ [2, 12]. Instant 5-sec evaluation!
2. VENN SET CALCULUS & CONDITIONAL CHAIN LAWS
2-Set: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)
3-Set: P(A ∪ B ∪ C) = ∑P(A) - [P(AB) + P(BC) + P(CA)] + P(ABC)
• Exactly 1 of A, B: P(A) + P(B) - 2P(AB)
• Exactly 1 of A, B, C: ∑P(A) - 2∑P(AB) + 3P(ABC) | Exactly 2: ∑P(AB) - 3P(ABC)
Conditional Probability P(A | B) & Chain Rule
P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B), for P(B) > 0
• Complementary Rule: P(A' | B) = 1 - P(A | B) ⟹ P(A | B) + P(A' | B) = 1
• EXAM TRAP: P(A | B) + P(A | B') ≠ 1 in general! Conditioning event is fixed.
• Chain Rule: P(A ∩ B ∩ C) = P(A) · P(B | A) · P(C | A ∩ B)
Biased coin P(H)=p, P(T)=1-p tossed until first Head. P(First head on even toss) = 2/5:
Partition B₁, B₂, ..., Bₙ of S (mutually exclusive & exhaustive, ∑P(Bᵢ)=1):
• Tree Diagram Rule: Sum of all branch path products reaching event A.
P(Bₖ | A) = [ P(Bₖ) · P(A | Bₖ) ] / [ ∑ᵢ₌₁ⁿ P(Bᵢ) · P(A | Bᵢ) ]
• Prior P(Bₖ): Knowledge before evidence A. Likelihood P(A|Bₖ): Evidence chance.
• Posterior P(Bₖ|A): Updated probability of cause Bₖ AFTER observing effect A.
• Denominator is always the marginal probability P(A) from Total Probability.
Medical Testing Screening Paradox (The Base Rate Fallacy)
Prevalence: P(D)=0.001, P(H)=0.999. Sensitivity: P(+|D)=0.90. Specificity: P(-|H)=0.99 ⟹ P(+|H)=0.01.
Why? Healthy population (99.9%) generates ~92% of all positive test results!
• Finite Discrete? (Coins, dice, cards, urns) ⟹ n(E) / n(S)
12 Face Cards (4 Kings, 4 Queens, 4 Jacks) + 4 Aces
GUARD: Check if P(outcome) depends on previous outcome!
YES: P(A ∩ B) = 0 ⟹ P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B)
NO: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A ∩ B)
P(Exactly 1 misses) = ∑ P(Eᵢ misses) ∏_{j≠i} P(Eⱼ hits)
P(Neither A nor B) = P((A ∪ B)') = 1 - P(A ∪ B)
P(At least one fails) = P((A ∩ B)') = 1 - P(A ∩ B)
• Difference Rule: P(A ∩ B') = P(A) - P(A ∩ B)
• Symmetric Diff: P(A △ B) = P(A ∪ B) - P(A ∩ B)
GUARD: Never add probabilities without subtracting intersection!
Identify conditioning event B: P(A | B) = P(AB) / P(B)
• Does condition occur AFTER the event?
S = {BB, BG, GB, GG} (4 equally likely)
P(Both Boys | At least one boy) = 1/3 (Condition: {BB, BG, GB})
P(Both Boys | Elder is a boy) = 1/2 (Condition: {BB, BG})
GUARD: Conditioning space B strictly replaces universal space S!
Identify exhaustive causes B₁, B₂, ..., Bₙ. Ensure ∑P(Bᵢ) = 1.
P(B₁) = 1/3, P(B₂) = 1/3, P(B₃) = 1/3 (e.g. 3 urns chosen at random).
Calculate probability of observed outcome given each specific cause.
P(A) = ∑ P(Bᵢ) · P(A | Bᵢ). Path product sum.
P(Bₖ | A) = [ P(Bₖ) · P(A | Bₖ) ] / P(A).
